q: anna j. mary booyzen 1914 - buried 23 jan 1914, brixton - d.r. section, grave 2472 · booyzen six months old - not "0 days", which is what the index says and what this archive printed for an afternoon. the register keeps years, months and days in three columns and the 6 sits in months. hers was a bought grave, marked private. the earliest booyzen burial this archive has found at brixton, and the beginning of a family plot that would take four more over the next twenty years. 

anna jacoba van der merwe - - - · kolbe she remarried, and her second husband is why she was hard to find. the free state archives hold her under a different surname: vab mhg m777 - "mccabe, anna jacoba. nooiensvan van der merwe. eggenote john gherson [kolbe]", 1896. widowed in 1868 with twelve children and dead twenty-eight years later as mrs mccabe. her husband's own estate is beside it - vab mhg k71, "kolbe, john gerson eleazar. eggenote anna jacoba (gebore van der merwe)", 1868. and the mccabe name is already in this archive: a rosa magdalena kolbe was baptised at bloemfontein in 1890 to frederik fortuna kolbe and maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe - a second kolbe-mccabe marriage in the same small free state world, and this archive does not yet know whether that is a coincidence. 20 september 2026 - it may not be one. on a geni profile, the frederik fortunata kolbe of that baptism is the commandant's own son, born 1857 at bloemfontein - so the commandant's widow married francis mccabe the landdrost about april 1871, and her son married a mccabe. mccabe died ten months later leaving "four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". the two households were one for eleven months, and a marriage across them afterwards is ordinary rather than remarkable. and this archive already held the other half without noticing. vab mhg c129, the 1872 estate index for francis mccabe, names his first wife as maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath - and the bloemfontein baptism of 1890 names the mother as maria petronella elizabeth antoinetta mccabe. the same four-part name, carrying mccabe as a surname: she is almost certainly his daughter by raath, named for her mother entire. so a stepbrother married a stepsister, nine years after their parents' eleven-month marriage, and mccabe's obituary had already said he left "four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". the one link that is from a user tree and not from a document is that her husband is the commandant's son; it is not adopted, and vab mhg c129 would settle it by naming the daughters. neither estate is read. m777 is the document that would name the twelve children. married john gerson eliezar kolbe on 3 april 1843 and was widowed on the same date twenty-five years later. she is the third van der merwe to marry into these families. 15 september 2026 - mccabe has a first name, a birth date and an office. he is francis mccabe, landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier, born at one of the military posts in what is now british kaffraria on 29 september 1817. his obituary in the friend says he "married his second wife about ten months since - the widow of the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", and he died suddenly of heart disease on the modder river road on 23 february 1872, aged 54, leaving "a widow, four sons and two daughters, besides a large family of step-children". so: married 3 april 1843, widowed 3 april 1868 with twelve children, married again about april 1871, widowed again fifteen months later, and dead in 1896 under his name. for about eleven months there were eighteen children attached to one household. she was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868, when a black mare and foal of hers were stolen - the court record that says so is the only document this archive has that shows her doing anything at all.

baba booyzen - - before 1940 · booyzen a twelfth child, and the only word cut for her or him is "baba". the centre pillar of the silverton stone lists twelve children by their household names; the 1940 estate lists eleven by their registered ones; and when the two are set side by side every one of the eleven is claimed exactly once, leaving "✝ baba" - a birth star, a cross, and no name - with nothing to match. not on the estate because the child was already dead when it was written. no date, no sex, no name, no order beyond the stone's own. this archive has met the shape before: joseph heinrich daschner's 1942 notice named eleven children and the brixton register produced a twelfth. a death notice lists the living; a gravestone, cut by the family, lists the children.

s: 29 Sep 1817, a military post in what became British Kaffraria – 23 Feb 1872, the Modder River road, district Bloemfontein · Kolbe
q: francis mccabe 29 sep 1817, a military post in what became british kaffraria - 23 feb 1872, the modder river road, district bloemfontein · kolbe the second husband, and the reason the commandant's widow is filed under the wrong surname in the free state estate index. landdrost of bloemfontein, son of dr patrick mccabe, a staff-assistant surgeon attached to the british army on the cape frontier; his mother rose died at bloemfontein on 1 august 1858, aged 72 years 3 months and 8 days. he married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 - "his second wife, about ten months since" - and was dead within fifteen months. on the anniversary of the state's independence he had spent the day superintending the burghers' annual target shooting for the government prize; at a quarter past five he set off by spring-cart for the diamond fields meaning to sleep at his own farm "uitvlugt" on the modder river; at about half past seven, in deceptive moonlight and one hour's ride short of the farm of g.f. enslin, the cart went into a sluit washed out by the rains. he was dead of heart disease that evening. he left four sons and two daughters of his own and "a large family of step-children", which is a newspaper counting the commandant's twelve. his brother joseph, the well-known trader and traveller, had died in the interior in december 1865; his brother john died at bloemfontein in 1860. he was buried on the sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried by the resident members of the volksraad and the principal government officers, with the state president and upwards of two hundred walking behind. 15 september, from the free state estate index. vab mhg c129: "mccabe, francis. eggenotes 1) maria petronella elisabetha antoinetta raath en 2) anna (gebore van der merwe)", 1872 - so he had a first wife and she has a name. and vab 1/3/1/12 bc11: "mccabe, francis. insolvente boedel", with the remark "bevat geen sterfkennis nie" - contains no death notice. the landdrost of bloemfontein, buried with the state president walking behind him and two hundred people after that, left an insolvent estate. his widow's own entry, m777, names both her husbands, so the remarriage is in the archives and not only in a newspaper.

"petition of frederick fortunatus werdmuller of malmesbury", cape supreme court, 1907, twice in one year, both times in other men's insolvent estates; and an estate of his own in 1953. this archive has already followed frederik fortunatus from kolbe (1839) to barry (1863) to booysen (1899); here it is again, on a werdmuller - and augusta louisa kolbe married a werdmuller. 17 september 2026 - he is shown to be her son, and the sentence above is withdrawn. the last 214 images of the burgersdorp baptism register hold his font: fredrik fortunatus steenkamp werdmuller, born 25 april 1861, baptised 19 may 1861 at burgersdorp, father coenraad johannes otto werdmuller, mother augusta louisa kolbe - familysearch 1:1:6fw6-wxgs, image 673. the settler's fourth daughter gave her child her brother's name, which is how frederik fortunatus reached a fourth surname. and it dates augusta louisa: she was bearing her husband's children in 1861, thirteen years before he married again at burgersdorp in 1874 - which bears directly on whether charles andrew was her son. the one step not taken: that the child of 1861 is the man of the 1907 petition and the 1953 estate. both are frederick fortunatus werdmuller at the cape and the name is rare; the 1907 man is of malmesbury and the child was baptised at burgersdorp, and no document read here joins them. 

frederick kolbe of 1816 bapt. 16 dec 1816, westminster - - · kolbe right surname, right parish, right decade, and a gap in the family's own baptism run exactly there. he is not a brother. his father is george and his mother elizabeth, and his register batch is c72301-7 rather than the family's c15051-2 or c06236-1. he was one click from being made an eighth son, and what stopped it was reading the parents' names on the transcript instead of the name, place and year in the result list. the same check threw out henry kolbe, baptised at southwark on 2 february 1800 - father henry, mother susannah. and the rejection turned out not to be a dead end. morning advertiser, 31 december 1832: "left his home, monday, december 10, frederick kolbe, about 16, dark hair and eyes, with an impediment in his sight. any information addressed mrs. kolbe, no. 18, gerrard-street, soho, will be rewarded; if he will return, will…" - and a boy "about 16" in december 1832 is one baptised in december 1816. gerrard street is two streets from church street. there were two kolbe households in soho at once, and every soho kolbe record on this site has to be read against that. whether the two families were related is not known here. 

frederik fortunatus downing kolbe 1891, wakkerstroom - 2 nov 1918, wakkerstroom - aged 27 · kolbe the man who proved the convergence. he carries both of this family's kolbe names at once - frederik fortunatus off his grandfather, downing off a london marriage of 1819 - and a london surname has no business in the eastern transvaal except through that wedding. born seventy-two years after it. married hester gerbina susanna joubert at volksrust at twenty-one, the clerk writing his second name as "daomig". dead at wakkerstroom on 2 november 1918, four months after his brother daniel, which is the influenza. 

s: 1839, Bethulie, Orange Free State – 23 Nov 1929, Utrecht, Natal — aged about 90 · Kolbe
q: frederik fortunatus kolbe 1839, bethulie, orange free state - 23 nov 1929, utrecht, natal - aged about 90 · kolbe the source of the fortunatus name across three families - and, as of 14 september 2026, a man with a household. the settler's tenth child, born at a mission station the year his father was working the orange river. he married elizabeth johanna du toit, and eight of their children are in the dutch reformed registers: baptised at colesberg in 1863, 1865, 1868, 1873, 1876 and 1877, at hopetown in 1870, and at bethulie in 1881. the eldest is a george augustus, named for the grandfather who had been dead nineteen years. then the household goes north: three of those children marry or die at wakkerstroom in the eastern transvaal, four hundred miles from the font. that is the second proof of the wakkerstroom convergence, and it does not depend on a name - it is a family moving. 17 september 2026 - he has a death, a district and an estate. pietermaritzburg estate files: "frederick fortunabis kolbe, born 1839 kaap provinsie, died 23 november 1929 at utrecht", probate 1929 - familysearch 1:1:qlr2-xfjc. ninety years old. and the estate names his children, the daughters under both surnames, which is how a daughter gets followed: george augustus, gabriel stephanus, martha angelina, margaret harriet kolbe van der spuy, frederick fortunatus, catharina maria louisa kolbe louw, elizabeth johanna kolbe pattison, petronella jacoba adriana kolbe beukes and adriana henrietta johanna kolbe oosthuizen. nine, not eight - the note above is careful and says eight are in the registers; the ninth is not. the file itself is not read.

g.a. kolbe of piet retief 23 feb 1836 - 7 jan 1913, piet retief · kolbe a date for the twin, if it is him. the stone at piet retief reads "vader en moeder - g.a. kolbe - geb. 23 feb. 1836 - overl. 7 jan. 1913 - a.m. kolbe - geb. 4 mei 1843 - overl. 21 sep. 1907 - van hun kinders". the settler's ninth and tenth children were twins born at burgersdorp in 1836, charlotte felicia and george augustus, and this archive has never had a day for either. a g.a. kolbe born 23 february 1836 is exactly the right man in exactly the right year - and it would date his twin sister too. it is initials and a year, not a name and a parent, and this archive has spent today being careful about exactly this. it would also give the other george augustus kolbe - born burgersdorp 2 october 1861, dead standerton 1934, buried wakkerstroom - a plausible father aged twenty-five, which is the shape the eastern transvaal kolbes have been missing.

s: 7 Dec 1802, Soho — baptised 2 Feb 1803, Westminster – 1 Dec 1844, “Wurtemburg”, Colesberg · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe 7 dec 1802, soho - baptised 2 feb 1803, westminster - 1 dec 1844, "wurtemburg", colesberg · kolbe his obituary is found, eighteen days after the death: grahamstown journal, 19 december 1844. "died at his farm, wirtemberg, near the orange river, december 1st, the rev. george augustus kolbe, aged 44 years, a man possessed of a most amiable temper, and of more than ordinary abilities. he was the last remaining of eight sons of john godloff kolbe esq. of brunswick-square, london, has left a widow and ten children... he having been for many years engaged in rendering them medical advice and assistance whenever called upon... his disease was an affection on the lungs." eight sons, seven of them dead before december 1844 and not one in this archive. brunswick square, which is not conduit street and is a mile and a half from it. a man who doctored a district for thirty years, where his own death notice says only "agriculturist". and a cause of death, after nearly a year ill. the notice also says 44 when he was 41, and ten children when this archive counts eleven living - it is the best kind of source and it is not a register. 1820 settler - the nautilus, owen's party, algoa bay 14 apr 1820. married at sixteen on a sworn falsehood, and the roll carries a second one: "kolbe, george augustus 20. chemist. w margaret 19", where he was sixteen and she was sixteen. he sailed from gravesend four days before his seventeenth birthday. the two lies do not even agree - nobody "twenty-one and upwards" in january 1819 is twenty in december. owen's party was 52 people, no. 3 on the colonial department list, joint-stock and recruited in london, and it collapsed in 1821 when thomas owen refused to draw rations and left; his brother took over and the party dispersed. he was eighteen, with no leader, no rations and no location, and the next record of him is the graaff-reinet mission three years later. preached across the orange river. his grandson could not name him in 1915. 15 september - he was an lms missionary, and his father wrote to him. the south african library at cape town holds msb751, the ga kolbe collection, donated by dr jean griffiths of somerset west in 1985: "george augustus kolbe, pharmacist, 1820 settler, missionary, married margaret downing" and, on a second entry, "george augustus kolbe, 1802-44. lms missionary." it corroborates a memory this archive published the same morning as an inference - john montgomery's recollection of a bushman mission school at koolskop about 1824, where colesberg now stands. two sources with nothing to do with each other, agreeing. the collection is four photocopied pages containing a letter of 23 august 1830 from johan kolbe in london to his son - the only known document connecting the tailor of conduit street to the settler of colesberg. it has now been read, and it does not carry a street address. the catalogue called it a letter "on his ordination" and this archive repeated the catalogue; it is not. 20 september 2026 - and a second attachment came with it. a two-page afrikaans typescript headed "msb 751 / [konsep] vir dsab / voorlopige teks", initialled ks and dated 18/2/92 - a draft entry for the dictionary of south african biography, by dr karel schoeman, on the word of the national library that holds the file: "the author, ks, would be dr. karel schoeman who worked here at the national library". it is a secondary work and this archive does not take secondary works as evidence - but it agrees with this archive on nine points reached by nine other roads (the 1802 birth, j.g.e. kolbe 1822-68 at leeuberg as a commandant, margaret downing 1803-1867, the 1819 london marriage, the apothecary's trade, the farm wurthemberg, ten children, philippolis from march 1831) and it is wrong about exactly one thing: it calls his father a german apothecary. he was a tailor, on 121 rate books, two printed masters' lists, three gazette notices, the census, the burial register and his other son's sworn deposition. the trade is the son's, moved one generation up. what the entry adds, all of it untested: the graaff-reinet missionary society from about 1824, working among the slaves of the district; acceptance as an lms mission assistant on 8 february 1828 and posting to boesmanskool - the present bethulie - with james clark among the san; a journey with melvill to the caledon valley in november 1828, as far as present-day ladybrand, the earliest journey in the present free state of which a written record survives, and printed under his own name in the transactions of the missionary society for 1829 - a second document he wrote himself, searched for and not found; philippolis from march 1831, alone after melvill left in march 1832; ordination on 25 may 1833 by the french missionaries arbousset and casalis; his advice behind the berlin missionary society's founding of bethanie in 1834; an accusation of adultery in 1836 with the wife of one of his congregation, agitated by h. hendricks, secretary of the griqua council - an inquiry by the french missionaries acquitted him - continued opposition from t. atkinson, withdrawal from the station in march 1837 and dismissal by the lms on 19 june 1837; and the farm driefontein near philippolis. it is also wrong a second time, and in its own first source: it says his death notice records only eight children. the death notice names ten, and this archive has read it, photographed it and published the transcription - kab mooc 6/9/35: 7698, signed m. kolbe at colesberg in january 1845. it also settles the farm name. this archive had wirtemberg from the obituary and knapdaar from the death notice and had quietly run them into one address; "wurthemberg, sometimes also given as knapdaar" is the statement that assumption needed. and it names a portrait: a likeness of him as a young man, in 1992 with c.j. du plessis of ruigtevlei, district bethulie, reproduced in olivier (1973); and a charles bell watercolour of a church service at philippolis in 1834 with kolbe in the pulpit, in the africana museum, johannesburg. this archive holds no likeness of anybody born before 1850. there may be two of this man. and he wrote something else, and it is findable. the 1829 journal extract the dsab cites is catalogued under the other man's name, which is why a search for kolbe found nothing: "extracts of the journal of messrs melvill and kolbe, addressed to the rev. richard miles, superintendent of the society's missions in africa, philippolis, 25 nov. 1828", in the council for world missions archive at soas - which is source 4 on the dsab's own list, two lines above source 6. an edited version dated 18 november 1828 appears in melvill (1829), and the journey is printed entire in karel schoeman (ed.), early white travellers in the transgariep, 1819-1840 (protea, 2003), p. 30. legassick quotes him: on the caledon they met people with "no other means of subsistence than the wild animals found in these parts". the first words of his this archive has read, and they are about famine. and the man he addressed it to is very probably the man who called at his father's house: richard miles was sent to cape town to act as dr philip's substitute while philip was in england, which puts him at the cape in 1828 and back in london by 1830. the 1830 letter says only "mr miles", so this is an identification and not a document. 20 september, later - and the society's own register has him, free, in eight lines. james sibree, a register of missionaries (lms, 4th ed. 1923), entry 278: "was previously connected with the graaff reinet missionary society, and laboured among the slaves around graaff reinet. was accepted provisionally by mr. miles, feb. 8, 1829, which action was confirmed by the directors, july 29, 1829. first laboured with mr. clark, at the bushman station, caledon river. thence proceeded to philippolis, arriving there, march 13, 1831. on may 26, 1833, he was ordained by the french missionaries, messrs. lemue, pellisier, and arbousset. his connection was dissolved by the directors, june 19, 1837." it settles mr miles - the man who called at the tailor's house in london was no messenger, he was the officer who accepted him - and it explains the father's adverb, because "provisionally" by miles and "confirmed" by the directors is precisely what "fully accepted" means. it disagrees with the dsab on the year of acceptance (1829, not 1828), the day of the ordination (26 may) and the men who performed it (lemue, pellissier and arbousset - no casalis). and it is wrong about a son. entry 522 calls frederick william kolbe, the rhenish then lms missionary of george and paarl, "son of rev. g. a. kolbe (no. 278)", where schoeman says he was no relation. schoeman is right and the society's own register is wrong: the arithmetic gave it away - a birth of 3 november 1821 against john gerson eliezar's 7 july 1822, eight months apart - and three works settled it. the new catholic encyclopedia calls his son monsignor f.c. kolbe "the son of a westphalian (german) protestant missionary"; s2a3 names him friedrich wilhelm kolbe, herero scholar, married at cape town in 1849 and at okahandja by april 1850; and the dsab had published its own entry on him in 1987. sibree has two kolbes in south africa and a compiler joined them. and his own journals are catalogued, in london. the council for world mission archive at soas, item-level: cwm/lms/05/05/100 - "extracts from the journal of john melvill and george augustus kolbe, during a tour to the north-eastwards of philippolis, 13-22 nov 1828", the manuscript behind the printed extract this archive hunted all morning; /102, extracts at philippolis 1828-1831; /106, journal, philippolis 1831-1834; /108, journal, philippolis 6 oct 1832 - sep 1833. six years of his life in his own writing, where this archive has held one sentence of his at second hand. and the year of the accusation is one box: incoming correspondence /044 (1835, which the catalogue says contains him), /046 (1836) and the 1837 file - 1836-1837 is box 15. and one likeness is catalogued, in scotland: university of edinburgh, centre for the study of world christianity, cswc 60 - five photograph copies of bell sketches of african congregations, item 3 "mr. kolbe… at philippolis in 1834". edinburgh calls him "a moravian missionary?", question mark and all; he was london missionary society, and this archive has his father's letter saying so. the dsab puts the original watercolour in johannesburg and never mentions scotland; edinburgh never mentions johannesburg. 

george augustus kolbe of bethulie 1869 - - · kolbe taken prisoner in 1901, aged 32, at sterkfontein in the bethulie district, and recorded as a free stater. tna wo 108/368 folio 581. sent to natal. the second man of that name in the same list - the first being george augustus kolbe of burgersdorp, whom this archive identified from the wakkerstroom stones. bethulie is on the orange river, in the country the settler preached across. and thirteen years later a g. a. kolbe of bethulie is president of the orange free state agricultural association. the british press, 26 june to 22 july 1914: "mr. g. a. kolbe (bethulie)" in the delegate list printed by the daily telegraph; "mr g. a. kolbe, president of the orange free state agricultural association and chairman of the orange free state delegation" at the royal agricultural society's show, in the western daily press, dundee courier, cork free press and exeter and plymouth gazette of 2 july; and on 22 july the daily malta chronicle has him sending a telegram of respectful greeting to queen wilhelmina on the delegation's behalf. same initials, same district, thirteen years apart - from a prisoner's number to the head of the free state's farmers. no descent from the settler is claimed here. 

s: 2 Oct 1861, Burgersdorp – 8 Nov 1934, Standerton — buried WAKKERSTROOM · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe of burgersdorp 2 oct 1861, burgersdorp - 8 nov 1934, standerton - buried wakkerstroom · kolbe the second george augustus kolbe of wakkerstroom, and the reason this archive had to withdraw a claim within the hour. his stone: "in liefvolle herinnering aan ons ouers - george augustus kolbe - geb. 2 oktober 1861 - oorl. 8 november 1934 - en susanna margaretha kolbe - geb. 26 oktober 1861 - oorl. 28 julie 1940 - hulle rus." born at burgersdorp, which is where the 1820 settler is buried and where the settler's twin son george augustus was born in 1836; the descent is not documented here and is not claimed. he is buried at wakkerstroom although he died at standerton, in the same cemetery as the other man of his name, two years apart in birth and twenty in death. and the birth date decides the prisoner: the 1902 pow record of wo 108/368 gives a george augustus kolbe of wakkerstroom aged 40, and a man born 2 october 1861 was forty from october 1901 to october 1902, where the other was thirty-nine all year. the prisoner is this man. 17 september 2026 - and now he has parents. the last 214 images of the burgersdorp baptism register, film 008039088, hold his font: born 2 october 1861, baptised 12 january 1862 at burgersdorp, father g. a. kolbe, mother anna maria viljoen - familysearch 1:1:6fwf-yvjt, image 685. the stone gave a date and a town and this archive wrote that the descent was not documented; the register gives him a couple. he has two younger siblings in the same book. whether his father is the settler's twin son - the g.a. kolbe born 23 february 1836, who would have been twenty-five - is the next step and is not taken here. 16 september 2026 - the pow entry now has a folio: tna wo 108/368 folio 709, the war office list of boer prisoners of war numbers 1-32,561, which records him as a transvaaler, residence wakkerstroom, and held in natal. he is one of six kolbe men in that list, and the only one of the six not in the southern free state. 

s: 29 Jul 1863, baptised 11 Oct 1863 at Colesberg – 28 Sep 1954, Wakkerstroom — aged 91 · Kolbe
q: george augustus kolbe of wakkerstroom 29 jul 1863, baptised 11 oct 1863 at colesberg - 28 sep 1954, wakkerstroom - aged 91 · kolbe the settler's grandson, carrying his name entire, and the man the wakkerstroom kolbes descend from. baptised at colesberg in the year of his uncle frederick fortunatus barry's birth. married martha sophia klopper, who was seventeen, about 1885; their eldest, maria johanna, was born at wakkerstroom in 1886. and his stone settles the identification beyond argument: "vader - george augustus - geb. 29 julie 1863 - oorl. 28 sept. 1954", which is the colesberg font date to the day. the 1902 pow record with residence wakkerstroom is not his: the other george augustus kolbe of that town was born 2 october 1861 and was exactly forty through ten months of 1902, where this one was thirty-nine. died at wakkerstroom on 28 september 1954, aged 91, which counts exactly from the colesberg font: born 29 july 1863, dead 28 september 1954. he outlived two of his sons by thirty-six years.

gerthardus lodewikus booysen - - - · booyzen the one document that names him has been weakened, and by somebody who had not seen it. on 14 september 2026 pieter van zyl, answering this archive's g2g question, guessed that the 1876 informant had reached for a name already in the household - and added, from memory, that he thought a child of petrus jacobus was called gerhardus lodewicus. he is right, and the child is on the same sheet: line 12 of that very notice names jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen among the eight children. so the name this archive takes from line 3, for the dead man's father, is the back half of his son's name, eight lines below, in one clerk's hand - and the half that is dropped, jan, is the name de villiers gives as the real father. this does not prove the father was jan and this archive is not swapping one unproved father for another. it removes the only document that has ever carried this name from the evidence for him. the top of the male line is now held up by less than it was this morning. he still has no birth date, no death date, and no parents: the oldest open question on this site is about him. 15 september 2026 - and the last escape route is closed. this archive's standing objection was that de villiers's 1893 original was revised by pama in 1981, and a revision can move a man; if the 1981 edition had relocated petrus jacobus, the death notice would stand. riel smit, who has the 1981 edition: "yes, de villiers & pama (1981) still place petrus jacobus (b3c4d7) b. 21 sept 1788 under jan b3c4." pieter van zyl adds that he searched for a marriage between a gerhardus lodewicus and a magdalena de beer and could not find one. four things now point one way and the only thing pointing the other is line 3 of notice 678. the spine is still not being moved on this: everything against him is a printed genealogy agreeing with its own earlier edition, and what he has is a primary document signed by a son. what ends it is the baptism entry of 21 september 1788 - the register de villiers compiled his entry from, naming the father in a contemporary hand. it is now the first item on the errands page.

s: 12 Aug 1887, baptised 27 Nov 1887 at Barkly East – 8 Dec 1956, Florence Nightingale Nursing Home — buried 12 Dec, grave 7110/1 · Booyzen
q: henry james booyzen 12 aug 1887, baptised 27 nov 1887 at barkly east - 8 dec 1956, florence nightingale nursing home - buried 12 dec, grave 7110/1 · booyzen and now there is a register. the g2g question this archive posted on 13 september was answered within eighteen hours by pieter van zyl, who put the baptism on the profile: "south africa, dutch reformed church registers (cape town archives)", ark 1:1:6kpt-t3z4 - henry james booysen, born 12 august 1887, baptised 27 november 1887, parents willem hermanus booysen and catharina maria sophia barry. verified here against the index directly. the 12 august 1887 has now travelled from a family tree, to a gravestone, to a church register, in that order, which is the wrong way round and is how it usually goes. the same answer also says he was a carpenter when he married and a retired miner of langlaagte estates when he died, of phthisis - and this archive has coronary pulmonary sclerosis off the johannesburg burial register. 17 september 2026 - the document is read, and both reports were wrong. his form of information of a death, south africa civil death registration 1953-1967, film 007751812 image 356, familysearch 1:1:6z9q-2tfg - the image itself, not the index. phthisis is on line 11, which is "pensioner or recipient of maintenance allowance". it is not his cause of death; part of them went on to south america in 1806 and came back to the cape in 1807; parliament complained in march 1809 that they had been sent "where they could have nothing to do"; a large reinforcement followed in october 1810; sir john cradock reviewed them and pronounced them "in the highest state of discipline"; a draft of 140 men embarked for the cape in october 1813; and then, in a letter from the cape dated 1 and 10 september 1817 and printed in five london papers that november, "the 21st light dragoons have embarked for india". he married at graaff-reinet on 9 march 1817. his regiment sailed for india six months later. a man who married in march 1817 and was keeping a house and a saddler's trade at cradock by january 1822 was discharged at the cape before september 1817, and what he was choosing between was a wife at graaff-reinet and a transport to madras. the town he settled in is named after the governor who reviewed his regiment.

he writes, and he signs himself. msb 751 at the national library of south africa is a letter of four sides headed "london august 23. 1830", opening "dear george" and signed "your affectionate father, j g kolbe". it is the first document in this archive he wrote himself - everything else is somebody writing about him. it does not carry a street address: the heading is "london" and nothing finer, so it does not settle brunswick square against conduit street, which is what this archive most hoped for. what it does carry: his son's acceptance by the london missionary society in the father's own words, dr philip carrying an earlier letter to the cape, mr miles of the society calling at the house, henry dying of dropsy and "resigned to the catastrophe", milne and elizabeth - "betsey" - removed to edinburgh, charlotte sending an evangelical magazine, a suit of black clothes sent out for a newly accepted missionary, the death of george iv and the french revolution of july 1830 as fresh news, and a request that his son fact-check a baboon story in a magazine. and the line that counts most: "kind love from your sisters & brother" - sisters plural, brother singular. of the eight sons, two were alive in august 1830. 20 september, read again from the file instead of from a mail preview, and it carries more. dr philip is not just the courier - "dr philip was exceedingly glad to hear of you being accepted by the l.m.s. as you may well imagine, he has promised to write to you a letter by the first opportunity". he sends a box: a suit of black clothes for george, and a jacket and waistcoat for john with a further jacket, "tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out". a year of newspapers, one number lost by henry. and the house has friends with names, the first in this archive who simply knew them: mr & mrs stanhope, mr and mrs warner, and mrs field and her daughters - "the eldest, miss mary, that was, has married a mr bellew, a surgeon". two of his four pages go on a story from the mirror about a scottish colonist near the xhosa whose wife was carried off by orang-outangs and recovered after two years as their queen - and he does not believe a word of it: "here we look upon the story as a fictious & romance… i should be glad to hear from you, whether that report may be founded in truth, or falsehood." a tailor of seventy, reading a cheap weekly, writing to the one man he knew who was actually there to ask whether it was true. 21 september 2026 - and the story is found, and he was right. it is "a singular letter from southern africa, communicated by mr. hogg, the ettrick shepherd", the mirror of literature, amusement, and instruction, volume xiv (1829), pages 313-318 - fiction by james hogg, author of the private memoirs and confessions of a justified sinner, printed as though it were a settler's letter home. every detail he recalled is in it: the chief karoo offering oxen and "a choice virgin to boot" for the settler's wife, "he foretold i should repent it", captain johnstone, the wife "carried across the river by a band of pongos, (ourang-outangs)", and her discovery as their queen. and the detail he got wrong is why five searches for it failed: he thought the colonist was called "either williams, or williamson", and the narrator is anonymous - it is his son who is called william. his first wife mary died 2 august 1814 aged 46 and his second, also mary, died 15 august 1824 aged 36, both buried in the german lutheran church register, tna rg 4/4631 - which is why one mary could never be made to fit a run of baptisms from 1792 to 1819. and the london gazette holds five notices, not the one this archive had. 12 may 1824 - the partnership of john gotlob kolbe and john henry kolbe, of church-street, soho, tailors, dissolved. 30 september 1836 - kolbe and david fletcher of conduit-street dissolved. 21 march 1845 - "john gotlieb kolbe and richard davies, of conduit-street, bond-street, tailors, has been dissolved by mutual consent", eight months before he died and still calling himself a tailor, which is what the obituary's "esq. of brunswick-square" has to be set against. 1824 was the year it all went: the partnership dissolved in may, his second wife dead in august, and his son in the insolvent debtors' lists in october and november. 16 september, later - and the 1799 tailors' list has a twin. in april and may 1834 the london press printed the roll of "considerably more than three hundred of the master tailors of the metropolis" who met at willis's rooms, st james's-street, to resist the grand national consolidated trades' union, and the entry reads "kolbe and fletcher, conduit-street" - morning post 30 april, globe 30 april and 10 may, old england 4 may, morning herald 10 may, london courier 10 may, true sun 10 may, public ledger 12 may. seven newspapers, one line. 20 september 2026 - and a historian called him an apothecary. the dsab draft entry on his son opens "die seun van j.g.kolbe, 'n duitse apteker wat in londen woonagtig was". the german is right and the london is right and the trade is his son's - george augustus sailed in 1820 as an apothecary, and the apothecary has been handed back up to the father. it is the only thing in that entry this archive can show to be wrong, and it can only show it because it read the rate books. it closes the gap: the rate books had him in soho to 1831 and the gazette at conduit street by 1836; he was at conduit street, with fletcher, by 29 april 1834. and it rhymes with the first list thirty-five years earlier - in december 1799 one of 234 masters over the combination acts, a young man at 18 broad-street; in april 1834 a firm with a partner and a bond street address, seventy years old, on the masters' side of the same argument.

s: 7 Jul 1822, Uitenhage – 3 Apr 1868, the farm Leeuwberg — aged 45 · Kolbe
q: john gerson eliezar kolbe 7 jul 1822, uitenhage - 3 apr 1868, the farm leeuwberg - aged 45 · kolbe the settler's eldest child, and until today a line in a table. his obituary - grahamstown journal, 15 april 1868, headed "death of commandant kolbe" - gives the whole man. born 7 july 1822; married 3 april 1843 to anna jacoba van der merwe; died 3 april 1868, on his wedding anniversary, at the farm leeuwberg, of typhus or typhoid caught on commando - "thus adding another to the long list of victims of our miserable war". he had settled on kaalspruit about 1850 and lies there - and he confirms the farm himself. a lost-property advertisement he placed in the friend on 9 march 1864 is signed "j.g.e. kolbe, kafferberg, kaalspruit" (the address as the paper printed it). the friend's own obituary transcription reads "[randspruit]", bracketed by the transcriber as doubtful; the man's own address settles it. that advertisement also puts the two brothers in one document: it concerns "a promissory note, date 9th march 1864, drawn by george augustus kolbe in favor of j.g.e. kolbe, payable 4 months after date for £154 stg" - lost on the market square at bloemfontein. he left a widow and twelve children - "of the eight sons and four daughters he has left behind him", which is the friend of the free state's own wording and a count the grahamstown reprint drops. only one daughter was married and the youngest child was an infant; two sons had been serving with him in the field and "proved themselves amongst the bravest of our burghers". none of the twelve is named and none is in this archive. 20 september 2026 - a collaborative tree names them, and it is not this family's own. a geni profile for frederik fortunatus kolbe, born 22 october 1857 at bloemfontein and dead there 18 december 1930, gives him as son of commandant.gen. john gherson eliezer kolbe and anna jacoba, and lists as his siblings catharina wilhelmina magdalena pienaar anderson, george augustus, general willem johannes, jan hendrik and petrus jacobus "and 6 others" - which is twelve. this is from a user tree, not from a document, and none of the twelve is adopted here on it - it is a lead and not a witness. but two of its claims match documents this archive reached independently: his wife maria petronella elizabeth antoinette and daughter rosa magdalene against the 1890 bloemfontein baptism already held, and his daughter maria margaretha downing rousseau against tab mhg 5450/68, an orphan index entry here that now has a father. vab mhg m777 is still the document that would prove them, and it is a better thing to order now that there is something to check it against. he was commandant of the district, a justice of the peace, a director of the bloemfontein bank and a deacon of the dutch reformed church, and he had spoken in the volksraad in may 1867. he had refused public life for twelve years after the abandonment, having protested the british withdrawal and applied to sir george clerk for compensation for his land so that he might leave with the troops; failing that, "he, like many more, had to cast his lot with the free state". and on his deathbed, in full possession of his senses, he told the doctor and the others present that this state had taken too much land from the basutos, that he had always thought so and had said so in the raad, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the governor for an equitable boundary. 20 september 2026 - a historian's draft names him too, and names the war. the dsab entry on his father says the eldest son "j.g.e. kolbe (1822-68), was later op leeuberg naby bloemfontein woonagtig en het gedurende die tweede sotho-vrystaatoorlog roem verwerf as kommandant". both years match this archive to the year - born 7 july 1822, dead 3 april 1868 - and both were got from an obituary and an auction advertisement that the entry does not cite. it is the strongest of the nine places where that entry and this archive agree from different documents. and it names what killed him: the obituary said only "our miserable war"; the war was the second sotho-free state war. and he may be in the 1830 letter, aged eight. read from the file rather than from a mail preview, msb 751 encloses "a jacket & waistcoat for john & a further jacket also for him, tell him his old father has sent it him, & to make haste to fill them out". clothes for a growing child, sent from soho to the cape in august 1830, when this man was eight years old and the eldest son of the house. if it is him it is the earliest document in this archive that mentions him. "his old father" is the difficulty and is not glossed over - the writer is his grandfather, and this is an inference, not a reading.

s: bapt. 29 Jul 1800, St James, Westminster – 13 Apr 1832, buried 22 Apr 1832, German Lutheran Church · Kolbe
q: john henry kolbe bapt. 29 jul 1800, st james, westminster - 13 apr 1832, buried 22 apr 1832, german lutheran church · kolbe one of the eight sons, and the one who lived longest of those found. baptised 29 july 1800, father john, mother mary, batch i02559-1. tna rg 4/4631 folio 100: died 13 april 1832, buried 22 april, aged 32 - twelve years before the obituary that counted him among the seven already gone. and he speaks. old bailey, session of 13 january 1819, trial t18190113-149 - richard kerr indicted for stealing "one coat, value 6l., the property of john henry kolbe". his own deposition: "my father is a tailor, and lives in church-street, soho. on the 9th of january, about eleven o'clock at night, i stopped at the star and crown public-house, westminster, and left my coat over my horse's head - i had a chaise standing at the door; i saw the prisoner go out, and suspected him - i went out, and missed my coat." not guilty. he was eighteen, and his brother george augustus sailed for algoa bay the following year. it is the only voice this archive has from the soho house, and it corroborates the rate books' address from a source that had no interest in it. and the london gazette says what became of him. 12 may 1824, issue 18027 page 796: the partnership of "john gotlob kolbe and john henry kolbe, of church-street, soho, in the county of middlesex, tailors" dissolved - father and son, in business together, at the address he gave the court five years earlier. then 9 october and 16 november 1824, issues 18069 page 1668 and 18080 page 1900, in the insolvent debtors lists, petitions to be heard at portugal-street, lincoln's-inn fields on 5 november: "kolbe, john henry (sued as henry kolbe), formerly of no. 22, norfolk-street, middlesex-hospital, and late of no. 4, mansfield-place". he was twenty-four, out of the family business and out of soho in the same year his stepmother died, and he was dead at thirty-two. 20 september 2026 - and his father writes about his dying. msb 751, the letter of 23 august 1830 to his brother at the cape: "henry had wrote to you himself & left his letter at the mission house to be forwarded to you… he keeps up pretty well at present, but what effect the winter may have upon him if it should set in very cold, as it did last winter, is perhaps not doubtful, since it must prevent him from taking exercise by walking, & which is a great means of keeping down the dropsy, of which he bears still the symptoms… i trust also that you will join your prayers, that he may vouchsafe to prepare him to a fit state of meeting his god… he appears at present to be resigned to the catastrophe." he had twenty months left. and the same letter's closing - "kind love from your sisters & brother" - makes him the last of the eight sons alive besides george augustus, so that the obituary's "last remaining of eight sons" became true on 13 april 1832, twelve years before it was printed. and he married three months after the trial: westminster marriages - john henry kolbe and matilda ford, 26 april 1819, st margaret westminster, both of that parish. he was eighteen. a mary ann maria ford kolbe married at whitechapel in the first quarter of 1847 - gro index volume az, 840, page 16 - and "ford" carried as a forename is how families carried a mother's maiden name. she is very probably his daughter. and the press gives his trade, which the gazette did not. law chronicle, commercial and bankruptcy register, 13 january 1825: "kolbe john henry, of norfolk-street, middlesex-hospital, last of mansfield-st., kentish town, tailor, draper" - so he set up on his own account in his father's trade, and the gazette's "mansfield-place" is mansfield street, kentish town. the may 1824 dissolution was reported in at least six london papers, all of them putting his name first: "j. h. kolbe and j. g. kolbe, church-street, soho, tailors". and the 1830 letter shows him doing an ordinary thing. packing a year of newspapers for the cape, his father notes one number missing - s: c. Oct 1874, Cape Province – 14 May 1940, East Lynne, Pretoria · Booyzen
q: stephanus francois booyzen c. oct 1874, cape province - 14 may 1940, east lynne, pretoria · booyzen the stone is now read, and it is the fullest document this archive has for him. silverton, pretoria, a double stone under one base reading booyzen: "'n simbool van liefde - aan my dierbare eggenoot en ons vader - stefanus francois - ✳ 29-9-1874, † 14-5-1940 - sy plek is leeg, sy stem is stil, ons swyg o'heer, dit is gods wil. ges. 75:1". his birth is now exact: 29 september 1874, where this archive had only "c. october 1874". and a pillar between the two halves lists twelve children by their household names - ouboet · ousie · bessie · betie · henna · evert · ✝baba · fanie · willie · pietie · johan · hennie - one of them marked dead with a cross. this archive had almost none of them. they are nicknames, not names on a register, and nothing is claimed from them beyond the count. his grave is found and photographed: "booyzen stefanus francois 1874-1940", silverton main cemetery, pretoria - a joint stone with his wife, "booyzen beatrix magdalena catharina nee boshoff 1889-1977". both dates match this archive exactly, and hers is the first death year it has had for her. he died at east lynne, pretoria, and lies at silverton. image located, not yet read. prisoner of war. a printed transport list in the pretoria government archives, image group 008019246, carries three consecutive booyzens shipped on the city of cambridge on 3 june 1901, all entered from pretoria: 18463 stephanus francois, 28 · 18464 petrus jacobus, 29 · 18465 david schalk, 54. consecutive numbers on one transport means taken together. age 28 against this archive's c. october 1874, which would have made him 26. the fuller register was then found, and it is better than the de list in every respect: item 1 of the same film, image 126, gives all three as living at pretoria, riding with the pretoria commando, and taken at tolosberg on 25 april 1901. its ages are 26, 27 and 53, which match this archive's own dates where the de list's 28, 29 and 54 did not. and then the prisoner number led somewhere else entirely. the medal-roll database at angloboerwar.com holds an entry for a stephanus francois booysen, burger, whose pow number is 18463 - the same number as the register - and it says he was a zarp, one of the zar's police, based at pretoria. quoting a city coins auction catalogue of november 2020 that described his abo medal and the papers with it: in action at talana, modder spruit, colenso, platrand (wagon hill) where he was wounded in the right leg above the knee, spion kop and dalmanutha - the zarps' famous last stand. his applications were completed by his commanding officer, commandant j. p. de la c. schroeder. he was one of forty-two boers taken at tolosberg in the waterval valley on 25 april 1901, with two guns and much stock, and was sent to india. this archive has not seen the medal or the application; it is strong secondary evidence tied to the register by the number and not by the name. what it does to the dispute: he is numbered 18463 and david schalk booysen is 18465, two apart on the same transport on the same day, and this man died at east lynne, pretoria, which is the district all three were taken in. that is a fourth point favouring david schalk as his father, and the first that does not depend on a forename. it is still not a document naming a parent. parentage disputed - see below. a son of the second marriage, and a messelaar - a mason, like his half-brother willem hermanus at indwe. his 1940 sterfkennis was fetched because it should have named his mother; his widow wrote only "oorlede" for both parents. married beatrix magdalena catharina boshoff at mosselbaai on 5 september 1905, certificate 1318 - he 30 and a jonkman, she sixteen with her parents consenting. eleven children; left immovable property and a will. the register gives his residence as pretoria, and eleven weeks later david schalk booijzen of goede hoop, pretoria - whose 1900 notice names an unmarried major son called stephanus francois - remarried in that same city. this archive placed him under petrus jacobus on his birth year alone. it is marked serious on the disputed page and it is not decided.

s: 23 Aug 1853, baptised 23 Oct 1853 at Burgersdorp – — · Barry
q: william barry 23 aug 1853, baptised 23 oct 1853 at burgersdorp - - · barry found twice in one day. he came in on the 1915 death notice of his mother margaretha kolbe, estate 1291, which names nine children where his father's names eight - and then the burgersdorp doopregister produced his baptism: william fredrik, born 23 august 1853, christened 23 october, godparents john kolbe, anna van der merwe and george kolbe. two of the three are his mother's brothers. a second william frederick thomas was baptised in 1861 and this archive cannot say whether the first died or a clerk erred - a doubt re-surfaced, and briefly mistaken for a new find, when the index was asked for every barry child of a kolbe mother. he is not on his father's notice, not on the cape rebel roll, and nowhere else in this archive. his father's 1903 registration said eleven children; with william there are nine named and two still missing. 

william frederick thomas barry 29 sep 1861, baptised at graaff-reinet - - · barry the other missing barry child, and he is invisible for the opposite reason to his sister. she has no surname in the index; he has the same name as his brother. william fredrik barry was born 23 august 1853 and baptised at burgersdorp; this william frederick thomas was born 29 september 1861 and baptised at graaff-reinet, eight years later, to the same parents - "margaret wilhelmina kolbe + john barry". a search for william barry returns the 1853 child and stops, and nothing in the result says there is a second. by this family's own practice the first william must have died - a baptism is not done twice, which is exactly what this archive concluded about the two catherine mary sophias. the "william who appears on nothing else" on his mother's death notice is one of these two and the notice does not say which. ark:/61903/1:1:623r-9mm9 and 1:1:62gj-sd8z.

s: 9 Jul 1847, district of Philippolis – 1941 — aged about 94 · Kolbe
q: williem johannes kolbe of panfontein 9 jul 1847, district of philippolis - 1941 - aged about 94 · kolbe taken prisoner in 1901, aged 54, at panfontein in the bloemfontein district, and recorded as a free stater. tna wo 108/368 folio 603. sent to natal. **and on 21 september 2026 the line in the prisoner list got a life.** he is **general willem johannes kolbe (1847-1941)**, who led the **bloemfontein commando** and commanded the southern districts of bloemfontein. **born 9 july 1847 in the district of philippolis** - the place his grandfather preached at, and where charles bell drew a kolbe in the pulpit in 1834. he was at the **siege of kimberley, where he was made general**, and afterwards at **paardeberg, driefontein and the brandwaterkom**, and he rode in **de wet's invasion of the cape colony in february 1901** - the year he was captured. **two horses were shot under him.** the french general de villebois-mareuil spoke of his leadership with praise; he was liked in his commando and is said to have treated the burghers kindly. **the source is printed, not a tree** - but read at one remove, and that is said plainly. the career above is in *afrikanergeskiedenis* (petronel fourie) and on the afrikaans wikipedia. **the pedigree below is on the wikipedia article only**, which cites **p. j. nienaber, *afrikaanse biografiese woordeboek* (voortrekkerpers, 1947), p. 139** and the fourie piece without saying which carries what; the fourie piece was read here in full and has no genealogy in it at all, **so nienaber is the source by elimination and his page has not been seen**. **and it names his house.** father **j. g. e. kolbe**, mother **anna jacoba van der merwe**, grandfather **george augustus kolbe, "a german missionary"**, grandmother **margaret downing**, the grandfather at **knapdaar, burgersdorp**, the home farm **onder-leeuwberg in the bloemfontein district**, and the father **a commandant in the basuto war of 1865**. every one of those is held here already and independently, including the two women's names and the farm the commandant died on. **the 1847 in the prisoner list and the 1847 in the dictionary are the same year, and panfontein and onder-leeuwberg are the same district.** **what is still not proved**: that the man in the prisoner list is the man in the dictionary. two documents agreeing on a name, a year and a district is strong and is not a register. **vab mhg m777**, the widow's 1896 estate, would name all twelve children - and so, in his own words, might *herinneringe van genl. w j kolbe* at the free state archives.

marico district · western transvaal a substantial booyzen farming district - and this archive can no longer say whose. seven booyzen claims for compensation as burghers were filed here in 1903-04, and the booyzen children who died in the johannesburg and vereeniging camps came from farms in this district. this entry used to call them "emphatically someone else's". that judgement rested on the belief that this family was in the cape until about 1907 - and the 1876 sterfkennis at rustenburg, one district east, shows it was not. no document links this family to any of the seven claims. no document rules it out either. unresolved is the honest word. 13 september 2026: and now a documented booysen marriage in the district. hendrik stephanus booysen - seventh child on the 1876 sterfkennis, son of the direct ancestor - married charlotta elizabetha dormehl at zeerust, the principal town of marico. it still links this family to none of the seven compensation claims. it does mean the last of the three districts has had one of these people standing in it, and the sentence this archive withdrew was wronger than it knew. 15 september 2026: the seven claims were pulled in full and the index line is the whole record - no farm, no forename, no amount. the same search turned up something nobody asked for: a jgl booyzen countersigning the subsidy application, the book orders and all four quarterly returns of a farm school at kwaggafontein in this district, 1898-1899. he is not identified. he is a candidate for the jan gerhardus lodewicus born 4 december 1855, of whom this archive has said for months that nothing is known. 

kwaggafontein farm · district marico, transvaal a farm with a school on it, and the whole of its correspondence with the government survives. forty-eight files in tab source od, from 4 october 1897, when g.e. ter haar of kafferskraal asked for a teacher, to april 1900, when the teacher asked for his money to be sent to the landdrost and the war closed the file. the teacher was h. de vries, fetched by wagon in december 1897. a jgl booyzen is on eight of the forty-eight - the subsidy application, the book orders, all four quarterly returns, the explanation of a £61-6-0 deficit, and a letter of may 1899 arguing that £8 too little subsidy had been paid. he is the school's money man, and he is not identified.

booysens suburb, johannesburg · witwatersrand not a family place - a trap. booysens is a mining suburb south of the johannesburg city centre, a couple of miles from forest hill and kenilworth where this family actually lived in the 1940s. it means every name-index search for booysen in johannesburg returns people whose only connection to the word is an address. the archive met it head-on: a death notice indexed under the surname daschner turned out to belong to charles bruce rennie, a miner of booysens, and nothing else about him touches this family at all. 

brakfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal the farm where the oldest document in this archive was written. on 14 september 1876, thirteen days after the death, somebody at brakfontein filled in sterfkennis no. 678 for petrus jacobus booijsen, aged 88, and wrote the names of his parents on line 3. fifteen years later it takes two more: his son's wife on 9 may 1891 and their son five days after her. and in 1892 hendrik stefanus, marrying again at zeerust, still gives brakfontein as his home - sixteen years on the same ground. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed. 

lichtenburg district · western transvaal where this family's western transvaal branch is, and it is a branch rather than a lead now. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen - fifth of the eight children on the 1876 sterfkennis, born district graaff-reinet about 1818 - died on the farm vaalbank in this district on 25 may 1885, estate tab mhg o/2899. his daughter magdalena susanna maria died on the same farm on 1 may 1920, and her sterfkennis names him. lichtenburg is one district west of rustenburg, where his father died in 1876, and one district east of marico. 

dugmore mine colliery · indwe, district wodehouse where a booyzen worked underground. the indwe marriage register of 21 september 1908 gives both bride and groom's dwelling place as "dugmore mijn" and the groom's trade as "mijnwerker". it is the only mine anywhere in this archive attached to a named member of this family, and it is coal in the cape rather than gold on the rand. the coordinates are approximate - the workings were at indwe and the exact site is not yet fixed. 

vaalbank farm · district lichtenburg, transvaal one farm, two deaths, thirty-five years apart, and the same family on it both times. jan gerthardus lodewikus booijsen - born district graaff-reinet about 1818, fifth child on the 1876 sterfkennis - died here on 25 may 1885. his daughter magdalena susanna maria, born about 1860, died here on 1 may 1920. it is the clearest evidence this archive has that the family did not merely pass through the western transvaal but settled in it, two generations before anyone reached johannesburg. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not yet placed. and a school on it. the education files of the south african republic hold a school at vaalbank, district lichtenburg, post office rietkuil, teacher j.p. louw, running through 1898 and 1899 - and the man beside the teacher on its money papers is written ds. booysen and ds booijsen. in february 1899 he wrote to the government to ask how school materials could be provided to orphans, arising from a case among them. whether ds. is a david schalk or the dutch abbreviation for a minister cannot be read off an index line, and six weeks earlier the same school wrote "ds van roojen" in the same slot. 

cherryville farm · district barkly east the third named barry farm, after manorowen and jerpoint. harriet louisa barry, eighteen, died here of typhoid on 7 september 1912 after thirty days' illness and was carried back to manorowen to be buried. her father, who signed the form, gave his own residence as manorowen - so cherryville is somewhere the family worked rather than lived, or another barry household entirely. the coordinates are approximate. 

slang river locality · north-eastern cape where dorothea regina barry, daughter of hendrik nicholaas barry and anna johanna maria schoeman, was baptised on 3 april 1892. from the index rather than the register, and placed only approximately. slangriverlocalitynortheasterncapewheredorotheareginabarrydaughterofhendriknicholaasbarryandannajohannamariaschoemanwasbaptisedon3april1892fromtheindexratherthantheregisterandplacedonlyapproximately

koedoesfontein farm · district rustenburg, transvaal where hendrik stephanus booysen died on 11 may 1908, aged seventy-nine, in the house of his son-in-law willem grobelaar. a farmer with no movable property, some land, and mutual wills with both of his dead wives. thirty-two years earlier he had signed his own father's sterfkennis at brakfontein, one district over. the coordinates are approximate. 

zeerust town, district marico · transvaal the principal town of marico, and the district this archive spent weeks holding at arm's length with the sentence "they are not this family, who were cape". hendrik stefanus booijzen married here on 14 april 1892 - 63, a widower of brakfontein - and signed his second wife's death notice here in august 1902. the sentence is withdrawn. 

s: Farm, Groot Marico · District Marico, Transvaal
q: driefontein farm, groot marico · district marico, transvaal charlotta elizabeth dormehl's own place. she gave it as her home when she married at zeerust in april 1892, and she died there on 6 february 1902 - three months before the peace, and ten years into a marriage to a man who farmed a hundred miles away at brakfontein. she never moved to him. the coordinates are approximate: the district is certain, the farm is not placed. 

zwartruggens town · transvaal where diederik arnoldus booysen was born about august 1887 and lived as a karweier - a transport rider. his 1935 sterfkennis is the first document in this archive printed in afrikaans rather than dutch or english, and it names his parents: ockert johannes stephanus booysen and elizabeth johanna sophia myburgh, both by then dead. zwartruggenstowntransvaalwherediederikarnoldusbooysenwasbornaboutaugust1887andlivedasakarweieratransportriderhis1935sterfkennisisthefirstdocumentinthisarchiveprintedinafrikaansratherthandutchorenglishanditnameshisparentsockertjohannesstephanusbooysenandelizabethjohannasophiamyburghbothbythendead

klerksdorp town · transvaal where ockert johannes stephanus booysen died on 16 january 1921, aged 69 - the man who signed his father's death notice in 1908 and who carried his mother's father's name out of the district of cradock and into the western transvaal. it is a civil registration and it names no parents, which is why this archive keeps going back to sterfkennisse. he has no estate file of his own. 

market street, pretoria street · pretoria, transvaal elizabetha margaretha booijzen, born marais, died in a zinc building in market street on 1 june 1900 - the capital's main street, four days before lord roberts entered the town. her husband david schalk booijzen, the direct ancestor's brother, did not file her death notice for three years and nine months, and against the question about movable property he wrote "none. compensation claim filed." 

turffontein suburb · johannesburg, transvaal 18 anderson street. richard peter booyzen, twenty-four, married, a sawyer, died here of influenza and pneumonia on 25 october 1918 after eleven days - the centre of black october, which killed some fourteen thousand people on the rand in six weeks. he was buried at brixton two days later. his birthplace on the form is the cape of good hope: born in the north-eastern cape, dead in a johannesburg mining suburb at twenty-four. 

mayfair suburb · johannesburg, transvaal this archive has had mayfair as a word on two pages and never as an address. kathleen barry died here in 1940. her great-granddaughter catherine mary sophia booyzen was married at st joseph's, mayfair on 15 january 1949 - the hinge into the lerena archive. and her son henry james booyzen was living at 3 15th avenue when he died in 1956. three generations in one suburb, and the cemetery register is what finally gave it a street number. 

roodepoort town · west rand, transvaal hendrik stephanus nicolaas booysen - baptised at rustenburg in 1882, dead at kempton park in 1959 - was buried in the central cemetery of the municipality of roodepoort-maraisburg on 12 october 1959, section i d.r., entry 96. this archive published him as buried at johannesburg for an afternoon because the familysearch collection carries that title for every register inside it. 

goedehoop place · pretoria, transvaal two men of this story lived here. charles petrus barend lowies, a hawker born in the district of cradock about october 1848, is "of goedehoop, pretoria" on his 1905 death notice - he died in the pretoria lunatic asylum on 5 june that year, leaving twelve children, six still minors. and david schalk booijzen, born in the district of cradock in june 1848, gives goede hoop, pretoria as his home on the register when he marries lowies's widow on 27 november, five months and twenty-two days later. this archive read that register first and wrote the address down without knowing what it meant. coordinates approximate. 

s: Hill, place of capture · Eastern Transvaal
q: tolosberg hill, place of capture · eastern transvaal where three booyzens were taken, and the only place on this map whose position this archive cannot vouch for. stefanus francois, petrus jacobus and david schalk booysen - prisoners 18463, 18464 and 18465, all of pretoria and all of the pretoria commando - were captured here on 25 april 1901, among forty-two boers taken with two guns and much stock. six weeks later they sailed from cape town on the city of cambridge. the hill itself is not on any map this archive has found. it is in no gazetteer reachable by search, in no battle list, and in no day-by-day war diary of 1901; the single source for the name gives only "tolosberg in the waterval valley, eastern transvaal". the pin is therefore placed at waterval boven, in the elands river valley - the waterval valley of the eastern transvaal, and twenty kilometres from dalmanutha, where the same man had fought the previous august. that placement is this archive's inference and not the source's. there is more than one waterval in the transvaal, including one in the lydenburg district north of here, and the hill could as easily be there. jeppe's map of 1899 has now been read and it does not carry the name. sheet 6 of the six-sheet map - the definitive survey of the south african republic, finished the year the war began - was examined over about twenty-five kilometres of the elands river valley either side of this pin, at full resolution. it names every farm with its number: waterval 161, kindergoed, elandshoek, eerste geluk, groot geluk, nooitgedacht, vlakplaats, kaalbosch, schoonspruit, kietspruit, weltevreden, treurfontein, uitkomst - and waterval boven and waterval onder stations on the delagoa bay line, with godwaan station east of them. it also names hills, in the form jeppe used: mauch bg., spitskop, tafel kop, peerds kop, zwart kop, zuikerboschkop, silverkop, vaalkop. there is no tolosberg among them. that does not move the pin and it does not prove the source wrong; it means the name was local, or was spelt otherwise, or was never a surveyed feature. the pin is still an inference - but it is now a tested one. 

knap daar farm · district colesberg the kolbe farm before wurtemburg. a land memorial of 1839 - cape town archives repository, lg 552, reference 664 - records "reverend g kolbe" asking that government ground adjoining his farm knap daar, in the district of colesberg, be surveyed and auctioned. this archive has george augustus kolbe dying at the farm wurtemburg in the same district on 1 december 1844, and knows he preached across the orange river; the memorial styles him reverend five years earlier and gives him land. the identification rests on an initial and a district, not on a full name, and the pin is placed at colesberg because the farm itself is not on any map read here. 

wakkerstroom town and district · eastern transvaal where the settler's family ended up, four hundred miles from the font. george augustus kolbe the 1820 settler died at colesberg in 1844 and is buried at burgersdorp; his son frederik fortunatus baptised eight children at colesberg, hopetown and bethulie between 1863 and 1881; and three of those eight marry or are found at wakkerstroom in the eastern transvaal. the eldest, another george augustus, was born at colesberg on 29 july 1863 and died here on 28 september 1954, aged ninety-one - a man whose life spans the whole of this archive's south african century. two men named george augustus kolbe lived and are buried here, born two years apart - 2 october 1861 and 29 july 1863 - and the older of them was the prisoner of war of 1902. two of his sons died here in 1918 four months apart, which is the influenza, and one of them carried the london surname downing into the eastern transvaal, which is what proved the connection. a woman named angeline kolbe died here on 15 november 1900, aged 28, and this archive cannot say who she was. 

s: Town, and a camp · Eastern Transvaal
q: volksrust town, and a camp · eastern transvaal twenty miles from wakkerstroom, on the natal border. frederik fortunatus downing kolbe married here. this archive also put a child's grave here for half a day and has taken it back: martha angeline kolbe, sixty days old, is buried at wakkerstroom, and the index that said volksrust was naming the district, which wakkerstroom lies inside. volksrust held one of the concentration camps, and the naairs index holds a camp grave for a g.e. kolbe, aged 35 - which is not the angeline kolbe who died at wakkerstroom in 1900, a different age in a different year in a different town. no person in this archive is yet shown to have been in that camp. 

s: Town, capital of the Orange Free State · Orange Free State
q: bloemfontein town, capital of the orange free state · orange free state the town the commandant's whole public life was attached to, and it took this archive until today to give it a pin. john gerson eliezar kolbe was a director of the bloemfontein bank, a justice of the peace, commandant of this district and a deacon of its dutch reformed church; he advertised a lost promissory note for £154 sterling on its market square in march 1864; he sat as foreman of the jury in a forgery trial here in 1866, before mr van soelen. his farm lay about two hours' ride away. and the man the free state estate index hides his widow behind was this town's own landdrost. francis mccabe, born at a frontier military post on 29 september 1817, son of dr patrick mccabe of the british army on the cape frontier, married anna jacoba van der merwe about april 1871 and was dead by 23 february 1872, of heart disease on the modder river road after a cart went into a sluit in the moonlight. he was buried here on the sunday afternoon at six o'clock, the coffin carried from the house by the resident members of the volksraad and the principal government officers, with the state president and upwards of two hundred people walking behind. 

s: Mission station, later town · Southern Orange Free State
q: philippolis mission station, later town · southern orange free state where the settler's children grew up, on the word of a man writing in 1868 who knew them. the obituary of commandant john gerson eliezar kolbe says his father "became a missionary to the griquas at philippolis, and most of his family, we believe, grew up there". this archive had reached the same conclusion from the children's baptism places - harriet hachilah machilah born here in 1831 - and this is a fourth, independent source for it. philippolis was the london missionary society's griqua station; george augustus kolbe was an l.m.s. missionary. 

s: Mission station, later town · Southern Orange Free State
q: bethulie mission station, later town · southern orange free state the other mission on the circuit, and a font this family came back to. frederik fortunatus kolbe was born here in 1839 - the source of a forename that has since crossed into four surnames - and johan casimir in 1844, the year his father died. forty-two years later frederik fortunatus brought his own youngest daughter, adriana henrietta johanna, back to be baptised here on 23 october 1881. 

uitenhage town · eastern cape the first stop after the landing. george augustus kolbe came ashore at algoa bay on 14 april 1820, and his eldest child - john gerson eliezar, born 7 july 1822 - was born here, forty miles inland. the family is at graaff-reinet by 1825. uitenhagetowneasterncapethefirststopafterthelandinggeorgeaugustuskolbecameashoreatalgoabayon14april1820andhiseldestchildjohngersoneliezarborn7july1822wasbornherefortymilesinlandthefamilyisatgraaffreinetby1825

s: Farm · District Bloemfontein, Orange Free State
q: leeuwberg farm · district bloemfontein, orange free state where commandant kolbe died, on the night of friday 3 april 1868, of typhus caught on commando. the pin was at fauresmith and it was wrong. it rested on a 1903 free state land file recording a "leeuwberg no 465, dist. faurismith" - a farm of the right name in the right province thirty-five years later, and nothing more - and it was published with its own objection attached, that fauresmith is a hundred and thirty kilometres from kaalspruit while the obituary says he died at the one and lies at the other. the objection has been answered against the pin. the friend of the free state of 13 january 1870 advertises for sale "the farm, wildebeestkooi, adjoining the farm leeuberg, the property of the late j.g.e. kolbe, about two hours ride from the town of bloemfontein". fifteen or twenty kilometres, not a hundred and thirty. the fauresmith farm is a different farm of the same name, and the two-farm contradiction this archive could not reconcile was never a contradiction - leeuberg and kaalspruit are neighbours. a man named jephts, described by the court as a man of colour, was living here in 1868 and owned a chestnut riding horse; it was stolen with two of the family's, and his name is in the record beside theirs. 

s: Farm · District Bloemfontein, Orange Free State
q: kaalspruit farm · district bloemfontein, orange free state his own address, in his own advertisement. the friend of the free state, 9 march 1864: a lost promissory note, £154 sterling, signed "j.g.e. kolbe, kafferberg, kaalspruit". the obituary of 1868 says he settled here about 1850 and lies buried here. the pin is at bloemfontein and it is an inference: a free state soil-conservation district is registered as "kaalspruit - kafferrivier (bloemfontein)", which pairs the same two names the advertisement pairs, in the district whose bank he was a director of and whose paper he advertised in. a name pair is not a survey beacon. the friend's own transcriber read this farm as "[randspruit]", bracketed and doubtful; the advertisement is why this archive reads kaalspruit. 15 september 2026 - the guess now has three documents behind it. the obituary of his second wife's husband calls him "the late commandant j.g.e. kolbe, of kafirberg, near this town", the town being bloemfontein. an 1870 auction advertisement puts the neighbouring farm leeuberg "about two hours ride from the town of bloemfontein". and his widow was living at springfield, ward upper modder-river, district bloemfontein in october 1868. kafferberg, kaalspruit, leeuberg, wildebeestkooi and springfield are one neighbourhood, and it is not at fauresmith. 

piet retief town · eastern transvaal two kolbe stones, thirty years apart, in a town forty miles from wakkerstroom. "g.a. kolbe, geb. 23 feb. 1836, overl. 7 jan. 1913" with "a.m. kolbe, geb. 4 mei 1843, overl. 21 sep. 1907", raised van hun kinders; and "p.j. kolbe, geb. 1_ aug. 1865, oorl. 28 nov. 1919". 1836 is the year the settler's twins were born at burgersdorp, and if that is him the stone dates a birth this archive has only ever had as a year. 

hoopstad town · orange river colony where the werdmuller line ends up. charles andrew werdmuller - second son of the man who married the settler's fourth daughter - is "charles werdmuller, j.p. of hoopstad" by 1909. his wife charlotte anne, born callaghan, died here on 17 february 1891 aged thirty-two, "after a long illness", having arrived "only a few months ago, in rather indifferent health", of a disorder of the heart that proved organic. she left "a husband and two little girls", and one of those girls married a holder of the victoria cross. 

steynsburg town · north-eastern cape where charles andrew werdmuller was living when he married, on 13 february 1884 - "charles andrew werdmuller, of steynsburg. second son of the late c.j.o. werdmuller, of burghersdorp". thirty miles from burgersdorp, where his father had been, and a long way from hoopstad, where he ended. steynsburgtownnortheasterncapewherecharlesandrewwerdmullerwaslivingwhenhemarriedon13february1884charlesandrewwerdmullerofsteynsburgsecondsonofthelatecjowerdmullerofburghersdorpthirtymilesfromburgersdorpwherehisfatherhadbeenandalongwayfromhoopstadwhereheended
